title: Etale transport and descent of a given universal first-order thickening
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $Z\xrightarrow{p}Y\to X$ morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with $p$ representable etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. A first-order thickening means a representable closed immersion whose ideal has square zero [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For $A\to X$, call $A\hookrightarrow A^+$ over $X$ universal if, for every first-order thickening $T\hookrightarrow T'$ of algebraic spaces over $X$ and every $X$-map $a:T\to A$, there is exactly one $X$-map $a^+:T'\to A^+$ restricting to the composite $T\to A\hookrightarrow A^+$. (1) If $Y\hookrightarrow Y^+$ is universal over $X$, there is an etale $Z^+\to Y^+$ whose pullback along $Y\hookrightarrow Y^+$ is $p:Z\to Y$, unique up to unique isomorphism inducing the identity on $Z$. The induced $Z\hookrightarrow Z^+$ is a universal first-order thickening over $X$. Consequently, if $Z\hookrightarrow W$ is any other universal thickening over $X$, its canonical map $W\to Y^+$ extending $p$ is etale and the square $Z\to W$ over $Y\to Y^+$ is cartesian. (2) Conversely, suppose $p$ is surjective and an etale map of first-order thickenings $(Z\hookrightarrow Z^+)\to(Y\hookrightarrow Y^+)$ over $X$ is cartesian. If $Z\hookrightarrow Z^+$ is universal over $X$, then $Y\hookrightarrow Y^+$ is universal over $X$. Fibre products are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. No formal unramifiedness hypothesis is needed beyond the displayed universal properties.

proof.text: First record the base-change facts used below. For any first-order immersion $A_0\hookrightarrow A$ and any $B\to A$, the ideal of $A_0\times_A B$ is the image of the pulled-back ideal; products of two generators are zero, so this is again first order. On every scheme base change a square-zero ideal lies in every prime. Thus the immersion is surjective, and the surjective-closed-immersion lemma makes it integral and universally injective. These are exactly the scheme-test hypotheses of integral-radicial etale invariance. The thickening base-change lemma also gives a homeomorphism on point spaces after every algebraic-space base change. In particular a map between two such thickenings is surjective if its reduction is surjective: conjugate its point map by the two homeomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 09ZX (lemma-base-change-thickening); the fundamental equivalence preceding equation-equivalence-etale-spaces; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals).

proof.text: For a representable etale map $E\to A$ and an affine scheme test $T_0\hookrightarrow T$ with $b:T\to A$, the pullback $E_T\to T$ is an etale morphism of schemes. By the definition of etale it is flat and unramified, so the cited scheme flat-unramified lifting theorem gives the unique section of $E_T\to T$ extending the prescribed section over $T_0$. Composing with $E_T\to E$ gives the unique lift. This also works for arbitrary first-order space tests: cover $T$ by affine etale scheme charts, whose reductions are affine closed subschemes. Apply the just proved affine lifting. On overlaps cover again by affine etale scheme charts; affine uniqueness equates the restrictions. Spaces are fppf sheaves, so these maps glue uniquely: after each scheme test of $T$ apply the sheaf equalizer to the pulled-back covering, and uniqueness gives naturality. The same chart argument shows that universality of a first-order thickening can be checked on affine scheme tests. Agreement of maps to $X$ is checked on these covers. All reduced tests are first order by step 1. This argument uses only scheme infinitesimal lifting, not the chartwise formal-etaleness theorem for spaces.

source.place: Tag 0603 (lemma-check-universal-first-order-thickening) and Tag 04AL (lemma-representable-property-formally-property), representable etale case, using more-morphisms.tex Tag 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale).

proof.text: Apply integral-radicial etale invariance to $Y\hookrightarrow Y^+$, with hypotheses checked in step 1. Essential surjectivity lifts $p$ to chartwise etale $q:Z^+\to Y^+$ with specified reduction $Y\times_{Y^+}Z^+\cong Z$. Full faithfulness gives exactly one isomorphism between any two such lifts inducing the identity on $Z$; its inverse lifts the inverse reduction. To prove $q$ representable, fix a scheme $H\to Y^+$ and put $H_0=Y\times_{Y^+}H$. Both $H_0$ and $F_0=Z\times_YH_0$ are schemes, the latter because $p$ is representable. Scheme thickening-site invariance lifts the etale scheme $F_0\to H_0$ to an etale SCHEME $V\to H$. Meanwhile $F=Z^+\times_{Y^+}H$ is chartwise etale over $H$ by permanence, with reduction $F_0$. Full faithfulness of the algebraic-space etale-object equivalence for $H_0\hookrightarrow H$ lifts the reduction isomorphism $V_{H_0}\cong F_{H_0}$ and its inverse, proving $F\cong V$. Thus $F$ is a scheme and $F\to H$ is etale, so $q$ is representable etale. The cartesian square gives a first-order $Z\hookrightarrow Z^+$ by step 1. This construction uses only the first-order immersion, not its universality, and applies below to test thickenings.

source.place: Tag 0605 (lemma-etale-morphism-of-universal-thickenings), proof (1), using Tag 05ZH (theorem-topological-invariance); representability checked with etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance), clause (1).

proof.text: Given a first-order test $T\hookrightarrow T'$ over $X$ and $a:T\to Z$, universality of $Y\hookrightarrow Y^+$ supplies the unique $b:T'\to Y^+$ extending $pa$. Etale lifting for $q$, extended to space tests in step 2, gives a unique $a^+:T'\to Z^+$ over $b$ restricting to $a$. Any other $X$-extension to $Z^+$ has composite with $q$ equal to $b$ by universality of $Y^+$, and hence equals $a^+$ by the same etale uniqueness. This proves universality of $Z\hookrightarrow Z^+$, without a formal-unramifiedness assumption.

For another universal $Z\hookrightarrow W$, apply universality of $Z^+$ to the test $Z\hookrightarrow W$ with reduction $\mathrm{id}_Z$, and universality of $W$ in the reverse direction. Both composites extend $\mathrm{id}_Z$; uniqueness makes them identities. Thus $W\cong Z^+$ compatibly with $Z$ and $X$. The composite $W\cong Z^+\xrightarrow qY^+$ is the canonical extension of $p$, since universality of $Y^+$ gives uniqueness for this test. It is etale and its reduction square is cartesian, since those assertions hold for $q$ and are preserved under the displayed isomorphism. This proves the remaining assertion of (1).

Now assume (2), and write $q:Z^+\to Y^+$ for its given etale map. It is surjective by step 1 and surjectivity of $p$. For a first-order test $T\hookrightarrow T'$ and $a:T\to Y$, set $U=T\times_Y Z$ and let $c:U\to Z$ be the projection. The etale-cover base-change theorem makes $U\to T$ representable etale and surjective. Apply the lifting construction of step 3 to $T\hookrightarrow T'$ to get representable etale $v:U'\to T'$ with reduction $U$; it is surjective by step 1. The immersion $U\hookrightarrow U'$ is first order. Universality of $Z^+$ therefore supplies the unique $X$-map $e:U'\to Z^+$ extending $c$.

source.place: Tag 0605 (lemma-etale-morphism-of-universal-thickenings), proof (2), construction of the lifted test cover using Tag 05ZH.

proof.text: First prove uniqueness of an extension to $Y^+$ for every test in (2), without assuming existence. If $b_1,b_2:T'\to Y^+$ are $X$-maps extending $a$, etale lifting for $q$ gives $e_i:U'\to Z^+$ over $b_i v$ with reduction $c$. The reduction compatibility follows from the cartesian given square. Step 2 allows this lifting for the space test $U\hookrightarrow U'$. Universality of $Z^+$ makes $e_1=e_2$, since these are $X$-maps extending the very same $c$. Therefore $b_1v=qe_1=qe_2=b_2v$. The surjective etale cover $v$ and the sheaf property imply $b_1=b_2$. This proves uniqueness on every test, in particular on the overlap tests needed next.

source.place: Tag 0605 (lemma-etale-morphism-of-universal-thickenings), proof (2): corrected uniqueness argument; representable lifting proved in step 2 using more-morphisms.tex Tag 04FF.

proof.text: Put $d=qe:U'\to Y^+$ using step 6. On $R'=U'\times_{T'}U'$ the two maps $d\operatorname{pr}_1,d\operatorname{pr}_2$ reduce to the same $Y$-map on $R=U\times_TU$: both equal $a$ composed with $R\to T$. The immersion $R\hookrightarrow R'$ is the base change of $T\hookrightarrow T'$, hence first order. Apply the uniqueness just proved in step 7 to this test and its common reduction to $Y$. This gives equality of the two maps to $Y^+$, although the two maps from $R$ to $Z$ may differ. The fppf-sheaf equalizer now descends $d$ along $v$ to $b:T'\to Y^+$. Concretely this is sheaf descent after every scheme test of $T'$, compatible by uniqueness. Its restriction is $a$ and it is over $X$, since both identities hold after the cover $U\to T$ or $U'\to T'$. Step 7 gives its uniqueness. This proves (2).
